x: from download to a working bot in about two minutes. dusk bot is a normal desktop app. there is nothing to set up first: no account, no card, no server. you open it, sign in to an ai you already use, and make a bot.

get the app from the download page . mac: open the .dmg , drag dusk bot into applications, and open it. windows: run the installer. it installs for your user only and needs no admin rights. linux: install the .deb on ubuntu 24.04, or run the appimage. the install page has the details for each system.

dusk bot has no model of its own. your bots think with an ai you already use: claude, chatgpt, gemini, grok and others. the first screen lists the ones it can use and walks you through setting one up. pick one and sign in the usual way. {{include ui-signin}} no subscription? an api key works, and so does a model you run yourself. see connecting an ai .

choose New bot , or press ⌘ N ( Ctrl N on windows and linux). give it a name, pick a shape and a colour, and tell it its job in plain words. one bot, one job. {{include ui-newbot}} you do not have to get the job perfect. you can change a bot's name, look, job and model later, and it keeps its chats and memory.

text it the way you would text a teammate. the thing you have been putting off is a good first message. "summarise what came in overnight and tell me what needs me." "find three flights to lisbon in march under €150." "read this pdf and give me the five points that matter." the bot answers in the chat and shows what it is doing while it works. it asks before the scary stuff: sending, buying, deleting.

make it a routine. say "do this every weekday at 8" and it becomes a routine . give it a computer. a bot can have its own browser and desktop that you can watch. teach it. tell it how you like things and it remembers . add a second bot. then put them in a group chat and let them hand work to each other. text it from your phone. see the phone app . everything so far lives on your own computer. nothing went to us, and

macos, windows and linux: what you need, how to install, how updates work and how to remove it. the app is one download for each system, from the download page . it brings everything it needs with it. you do not install node, docker or anything else to run it on your own computer.

you need macos 12 or later. there is one build for apple silicon and one for intel. open the .dmg you downloaded. drag dusk bot into your applications folder. open it from applications. the mac app is signed and notarized.

you need windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. run DuskBot-setup.exe . it installs for your user only, so it does not ask for an admin password. open dusk bot from the start menu. if windows shows a blue "windows protected your pc" box the first time, choose More info , then Run anyway .

you need ubuntu 24.04, 64-bit, with the gnome desktop. linux is still in beta. the .deb is the one we recommend. it installs what the app needs and sets up the sandbox for the bots' browser: sudo apt install ./DuskBot-amd64.deb or run the appimage, which installs nothing on your system: chmod +x DuskBot.AppImage ./DuskBot.AppImage two things work differently on linux today: a bot can control this computer only on an

the app looks for a new version once a day and tells you when there is one. nothing installs by itself. the note opens the download page , and you install the new version over the old one. your bots, chats and settings stay where they are. you can see what changed in what's new , and which version you have under Settings , then About .
on your own computer, everything dusk bot stores lives in one folder called .duskbot in your home folder: bots, chats, memory, settings. privacy and where data lives has the whole picture.

mac: quit the app and drag it from applications to the trash. windows: remove dusk bot from Settings , Apps . linux: remove the package you installed, or delete the appimage. removing the app leaves the .duskbot folder alone, so a reinstall picks up where you left off. delete that folder too if you want everything gone. make a backup first if you might want it back.
every release lists the sha-256 fingerprint of each installer. the download page shows the command for each system.

sign in with the ai you already use, add an api key, or point dusk bot at a model you run yourself. dusk bot does not ship a model of its own. every bot thinks with an ai you choose. you connect one once and every bot can use it.

you sign in to the ai yourself, on the machine your bots run on, the same way you sign in to that ai anywhere else. when a bot works, its messages go straight from that machine to the ai provider, under your account and on your plan. they do not pass through us. so there are two things to know: your plan's limits are the limits. a bot that works all day uses your ai plan all day. the provider's rules apply. their ter

this is the usual way. open the app and it shows the ais it can use. choose one and follow its sign-in. {{include ui-signin}} dusk bot works with claude , chatgpt , gemini and grok , and also with cursor, copilot, deepseek, kimi, qwen, opencode and cline. you manage them all under Settings , Model providers . you can connect more than one. then each bot can use a different one.

if you would rather pay per use, add a key under Settings , API keys . you can add a key from anthropic or xai, or from any service that speaks the openai api, such as openrouter, groq or together. paste the key once. it saves and checks itself, and the models show up in the model picker. keys are stored on the machine your bots run on. after you save one, the app only ever shows that a key is set. it never shows the

h: use a model you run yourself
x: local models work too. start ollama or lm studio, then open a bot's model picker and choose Use a local model . for any other server that speaks the openai api, add it under Settings , API keys as an openai-compatible server and give it the address. for ollama that is: http://localhost:11434/v1 local models can be slow to answer on a small computer. there is a setting for how long the app waits for the next words of

h: a different ai for each bot
x: open a bot and use its model picker. you can give your researcher one model and your code reviewer another, and change your mind at any time, even in the middle of a conversation. {{include ui-models}} when you swap a bot's model, the bot keeps its chats, its files and its memory. only the thinking changes.

Settings , Usage shows how much of your plan you have used, once a signed-in plan like claude or chatgpt reports it. api keys and local models have no limit to show there. if a bot stops because your plan ran out, it says so in the chat. wait for the limit to reset, or switch that bot to another ai and carry on.

h: on a server or a cloud computer
x: when your bots live on your own server or on dusk cloud , the ai is signed in there, not on your laptop. the app walks you through it from your own computer, so you never type a password on the server.

what a bot is, how to make one, and how to give it a job, a look and a model of its own. a bot is a teammate with one job. it has a name, its own chat, its own memory, and the ai you picked for it. you text it, it works, it tells you what it did.

choose New bot or press ⌘ N ( Ctrl N on windows and linux). {{include ui-newbot}} name it. anything you like. there is a button for a random name if you are stuck. pick a shape and a colour. this is how you spot it in the sidebar. tell it its job. plain words are best: "you read my inbox every morning and tell me what needs me." that is enough to start. everything else has a sensible default, and you can change all o

the job is the most useful thing you write. a few habits help: one bot, one job. a researcher, an inbox helper, a bookkeeper. a bot that does everything does nothing well. say what done looks like. "come back with sources, a table and a straight answer." say what it must not do. "never post anything until i say so." start small. start with one bot and hire as you go. some jobs people give their bots: bot job research

a bot's picture is a simple character: one shape in one colour, with two eyes. open the bot's settings to change the Character shape and the Character color . if you would rather use a picture of your own, upload one. png, jpeg, gif and webp work, up to 10 mb.
every bot has its own model. open the bot and use the model picker. you can change it at any time and the bot keeps its chats, files and memory. see connecting an ai .

under Settings , your profile has an About me box. what you write there is shared with every bot, in private chats and in group chats. it is the place for things all of them should know: your name, your time zone, how you like to be written to. things only one bot needs to know belong in that bot's memory .

bots sit in the sidebar like chats in a messaging app. right-click one to: pin it to the top mark it unread edit its profile duplicate it hide it, or delete it deleting a bot deletes its routines too. if you only want it out of the way, hide it. ⌘ 1 to ⌘ 9 jump to the first nine bots in the sidebar, and ⌘ K opens a switcher that also searches your chats. all the keys are on the keyboard shortcuts page.

texting a bot, stopping or steering it while it works, sending it files, and finding what it made. you talk to a bot the way you text a person. type what you need and press Return . there is no special syntax to learn.

a reply streams in as it is written. when the bot uses a tool, runs a command or opens a page, the chat shows a small line saying so. you can open it to see what happened. you do not have to wait for it to finish: send another message. a message you send while the bot works either steers it, so it reads your message and adjusts, or waits in a queue until the bot is done. one of the two is the default, and ⌘ Return do

h: when a bot asks you something
x: sometimes a bot needs a yes before it goes on: to send an email, run a command, or change a file. the question shows as a card in the chat with Allow and Deny . the bot waits until you answer. {{include ui-approval}} how often a bot asks is up to you. see permissions and safety .
drop a file onto the chat, or use Attach files in the message box. the bot can read documents, look at pictures and work with what you give it.

when a bot writes a report, a spreadsheet or code, the chat shows the file and you can open it from there. where the file itself lives depends on where the bot lives : on your computer: in the bot's own folder on your disk. you can also give a bot a project folder to work in. on dusk cloud: on your cloud computer, and a copy comes down to Documents/Dusk Bot , in a folder for each bot and conversation. see dusk cloud
a bot can keep several threads, so a long project does not bury a quick question. each thread has its own history. the bot's memory and job are shared across all of them.
⌘ F finds text in the conversation you have open. ⌘ K opens the switcher. it jumps to any bot or group chat, and it searches what was said across all of them.
press the speaker on any reply to hear it, or call a bot and talk. see voice and calls .

every bot keeps notes on how you like things done. the notes are plain files you can read, edit and delete. a bot remembers between conversations. tell it once that you only fly in an aisle seat, and next month it still knows. it does this by keeping notes, and the notes are yours. {{include ui-notes}}

what you tell it to. "remember that dana signs off on anything over €500." what it notices. when a chat goes quiet, the bot looks back over it and writes down new facts worth keeping: a preference, a decision, who is who. a note it picked up this way is marked as noticed. what it did. a short daily log of its work, in its own words. the log is for you to read. it is not loaded into conversations. a bot is careful abo

open a bot's settings and choose Memory . you see every note, and you can: tap a note to forget it type into Tell [name] something to remember to add one edit the notes directly undo any change from the list of recent changes the same panel has Show in Finder and Open in Obsidian (or your file manager on windows and linux), because the notes are ordinary markdown files in a folder: .duskbot/workspaces/<bot>/ MEMORY.m

the first 200 lines of MEMORY.md (or the first 24 kb, whichever comes first) are given to the bot at the start of every turn. the memory panel shows a gauge of how full that is. you do not have to prune it. when a new note would push the file past its budget, the oldest notes move to archive.md on their own. notes you wrote by hand stay put. longer notes on one subject live in their own topic file. before each reply,
some facts stop being true. a note can carry an end date ("until 2026-09-28"), and it stops loading the day after. birthdays and other yearly dates never expire.
anything that looks like a password, an api key or a token is blanked out before a note is saved. a bot that reads a key in a file does not get to keep it in its memory.
the Let this bot use memory switch is on by default. turn it off and the bot stops loading its notes, stops adding to them and stops searching them. the files stay on disk for you.

a bot does not learn from group chats unless you turn on Learn from group chats , which is off by default. when it is on, what you say in a group counts as yours, and what another bot says only counts if it is something that was checked or that you agreed to.
things every bot should know about you go in About me in settings, not in one bot's memory. see bots .

put several bots in one thread and they hand work to each other. you step in when one of them needs a yes. a group chat is a thread with more than one bot in it. it is for work that passes between jobs: one bot fixes the bug, another writes the post about it, a third emails the list. {{include ui-room}}

in the sidebar, find Group chats and choose New group chat . give it a name. a project name works well: "website launch". tick the bots that belong in it and choose Create group chat . group chats are made of bots, so you need at least one bot first. you can add or remove bots later, and rename or delete the group from its menu.

when you write to a group without naming anyone, the group needs to know who should pick it up. each group has one of these behaviours: behaviour what happens to a plain message Everyone responds it goes to every bot at once and they answer side by side. Only when mentioned nobody answers unless you @mention them. Leader it goes to one bot you chose as the lead, who hands out tasks to the others. an @mention always w

h: bots handing work to each other
x: bots in a group can @mention one another, and that is how work moves along. a bot finishes its part, tags the next one, and that bot starts. when a bot needs a yes from you it tags you, and the question waits in the chat until you answer. each bot keeps using its own model, its own computer and its own permissions inside a group. putting a careful bot in a room with a bold one does not make the careful one bold.

a group can have instructions of its own that every bot in it follows, on top of each bot's own job. open the group's panel to write them, and press ⌘ Return to save. good things to put there: what the project is, where the files live, how you want updates. you can also pin a message to the top of a group, so the one thing everyone needs stays in view.
deleting a group chat deletes its messages and every thread in it, and turns off the routines that run there. the bots themselves are not deleted.

have a bot read its replies aloud, talk to it instead of typing, or call it and have a conversation. bots can talk. you can listen to what ran overnight while you make breakfast, or call a bot and talk a problem through.

press the speaker on any reply and the bot reads it to you. you can also switch a bot to read every answer aloud as it arrives. a reply is tidied up before it is spoken. the bot says the words and names the files, and skips the code and the punctuation that only make sense on a screen.

choose call and it becomes a conversation. the bot hears you, tells you what it is doing while it works, and asks for approvals out loud. while you are on a call: hold the talk key to speak. you choose the key in settings. Space interrupts the bot. Esc hangs up.

open a bot's settings and look for Voice & alerts . give each bot its own voice and a group chat stops sounding like one person. voices come from one of these: voice what it needs built-in mac voices nothing. they are part of macos. elevenlabs an elevenlabs api key fish audio a fish audio api key grok (xai) an xai api key chatterbox a chatterbox server you run yourself you paste a key once and every bot can use it. l

the microphone in the message box turns what you say into text. on a mac it listens on the device, with apple's own speech recognition. nothing is sent anywhere. on windows and linux it uses fish audio's speech-to-text, with the same fish audio key as the voices. speech costs are billed by whichever voice service you chose, on your own key. the built-in mac voices and a local chatterbox server cost nothing.

ask once and a bot does it on a schedule, or the moment something happens. routines run while you sleep. a routine is a job a bot does without being asked again. "every weekday at 8, summarise my inbox." "when a new github issue opens, triage it." {{include ui-routine}}

just say it in the chat: "summarise my inbox every weekday at 8." "check competitor prices every monday at 9 and tell me what changed." "prepare the sales report at 9 on the first of every month." the bot sets the routine up in that same reply. a card appears in the chat showing the schedule, the time zone and the next few times it will run, with Edit , Pause and Undo .

Automations in the sidebar lists every routine, with a calendar and the history of each run. each bot's own routines are also in its panel, where every routine has a switch to pause it and turn it back on. you can also make a routine by hand there with New . the form offers the common schedules: every day, every weekday, every week, every hour, or once.

you say what you get "tomorrow at 3pm" it runs once. afterwards it reads Done . "every weekday at 8" it runs on the days you named. "every 30 minutes" it runs on a timer, anywhere from every 5 minutes to once a day. "the first of every month", "the last friday" a calendar rule. ask for these in chat and the bot works out the rule. a few details worth knowing: every routine has a time zone, and it keeps that zone even

a routine does not need a clock. it can start when something happens: in a connected app. "whenever i get an email from acme, draft a reply." "when a github issue opens, triage it." this needs the app to be connected . gmail is checked every 15 minutes. slack, github and most others arrive at once. when another service calls an address. the bot makes a webhook, and you paste its address into the other service. only y

h: the computer has to be on
x: routines run inside dusk bot, wherever your bots live. this matters most on your own computer: if the computer is asleep, or the app is closed, nothing runs. while it is plugged in, the app keeps the computer from dozing off for the hour before a routine is due. you can turn that off under Keep this computer awake for scheduled automations . a closed lid still sleeps. if a run was missed by less than 12 hours, it run
a routine follows the same permissions as its bot. if a run reaches something it must ask about, it waits. you get a notification that names the routine, and the card says what it is waiting for.

a run that trips over something passing, like the ai being busy for a moment, tries once more by itself. if it fails again you are told why, and the history in Automations shows what happened to every run. if your ai plan ran out, the run does not keep retrying. you get one notification saying what to do.
turn a routine off with its switch and it keeps its schedule for later. deleting a bot deletes its routines. deleting a group chat turns off the routines that run there.

a bot can have its own browser and desktop to sign in to and click through. watch it live, and take the mouse back whenever you like. some jobs cannot be done with words alone. holding a fare, filling in a form, checking a dashboard that has no api: these need a screen. so a bot can have a computer of its own. {{include ui-computer}}

a bot's computer is a real desktop with a browser. the bot looks at the screen, moves the pointer, types, and reads what comes back, the same way you would. it is separate from your own desktop, so a bot can work there without getting in your way.

this depends on where your bots live . your bots are a bot's computer is on dusk cloud a bot computer on your cloud. plus runs two at a time and pro runs five. on your own server a private desktop for each bot on that server. on your computer a cloud or server desktop if you have one. on a mac, a bot can also be pointed at this computer itself. letting a bot use your own computer is a bigger step than giving it one o

open the bot's panel and choose Screen . you see the bot's desktop live while it works. the same picture shows up in the chat when the bot takes a screenshot of what it did. the panel has more tabs: Browser for the bot's browser, Files for what it has made, and Routines for its schedules.

you can step in at any moment. choose Take control . click and type on the bot's desktop yourself. while you have it, the bot's own clicks and keystrokes are refused. choose Hand control back when you are done. this is how you get a bot past the things only you should do: a sign-in, a captcha, a two-step code. if you take over a bot's browser and then walk away, control goes back to the bot by itself after five minut

a bot stays signed in on its own computer, the way you stay signed in on yours. to sign it in somewhere: ask the bot to open the site, or open it yourself from the Browser tab. choose Take control and sign in. hand control back. the bot never needs to know the password. if you use 1password, you can also let bots use logins from one vault you choose, under Settings , Logins .

a computer nobody is using goes to sleep, and wakes when a bot needs it. waking takes a moment. on the pro plan your bot computers are first in line to wake. a bot only wakes its computer when the task needs a screen. a quick question does not.

a bot has one desktop, even if it has several conversations going. the first conversation that reaches for the screen gets it. another that needs it shows a line saying it is waiting for its turn, and carries on by itself when the screen is free.
a bot with a computer follows the same permissions as it does everywhere else, and it asks before the scary stuff. you can watch at any time, take over at any time, and stop the bot with ⌘ . .

the scary stuff. what a bot may do without asking, what it must ask about, and how you stay in charge. a bot that can click, type and send things for you needs rules. dusk bot has two: how much a bot may do without asking, and whether it may send things in your name.

when a bot reaches something it has to ask about, it stops and shows a card in the chat. you choose Allow or Deny , and the bot carries on or does something else. {{include ui-approval}} for some requests you can also allow that exact thing from now on, so a bot stops asking about a command it runs every day. the grant is narrow: it covers that one command or tool, not everything like it. approvals reach you wherever

every bot has an approval level. it decides what the bot does without asking. {{include ui-levels}} level what the bot does Ask for approval asks before it runs a command or changes a file. Auto-accept edits changes files without asking. other actions can still ask. Approve for me the ai's own automatic review approves routine actions and asks you about the rest. Full access does commands, edits and computer actions

for a bot: open its settings. the level applies to the bot and all of its conversations. for one conversation: use the level control by the message box. for a whole department: if you sort your bots into departments in the sidebar, a department's menu has Set for all bots in this department . it shows you what each bot will get before anything changes. you can change the level while a bot is working. it applies from

sending is treated separately, because a sent email cannot be unsent. this covers emails, messages, posts, invites and payments made through connected apps . reading and drafting never count. {{include ui-sending}} Ask every time: every send waits for your tap. Allow a daily amount: sends go out on their own, up to a cap you set. after that, the bot asks. you set this for each bot, in its permissions.

h: what a bot never needs to ask about
x: a bot can always read its own things: its job, its notes and its own conversation folders. that is its own notebook, not yours.

even Full access is only about approval prompts. it does not: sign in for you, or get past a captcha or a two-step code get around your operating system's privacy settings give a bot access to an app you did not connect, or to someone else's workspace turn on a feature you turned off

stop: ⌘ . stops the bot you are looking at. ⌥ ⌘ . stops all of them. watch: a bot's computer is live on your screen whenever you want to look. take over: Take control hands you the mouse, and the bot's own clicks are refused until you hand it back. limit what it can reach: a bot can only use the apps you connected and allowed for it. you are responsible for what your bots do and for what you approve. read a card befo

plug your bots into gmail, slack, github, notion and 60+ other apps, or add any mcp server yourself. a connected app lets a bot work inside a tool you already use: read the inbox, check the calendar, open the pull request, update the page. you connect an app once, and choose which bots may use it.

open Connected apps in the sidebar. find the app and choose to connect it. sign in to that app and approve what it asks for. this is the app's own sign-in page, so your password goes to them, not to a bot. there are 60+ apps to start with, including: {{chips gmail calendar drive docs sheets slack notion github linear figma stripe discord hubspot airtable asana trello dropbox outlook shopify sentry vercel supabase pos

x: connecting an app does not hand it to every bot. each bot has a switch for connected apps in its access settings, and you pick what it can reach. your bookkeeper does not need your slack.

h: what a bot does with an app
x: anything you could ask a teammate with access to do: "what is on my calendar tomorrow, and is there time for lunch?" "find the latest invoice from acme in my email and file it in drive." "open an issue in linear for the checkout bug and assign it to me." reading and drafting happen freely. sending is different: emails, messages, posts and payments follow the bot's sending on your behalf setting.

h: start a routine from an app
x: a connected app can also wake a bot up. "whenever i get an email from acme, draft a reply." "when a github issue opens, triage it." these are routines that start from something happening in an app instead of from a clock.

if a tool you use is not on the list, you can add it yourself as an mcp server. mcp is an open way for ai apps to use tools, and many services now offer one. open Plugins , then MCP servers , and choose Add server . paste what you were given into the one box. it understands a link to the server, a claude mcp add command, an npx , uvx or docker run line, or a block of mcpServers json. the app works out the name and th
disconnect an app from Connected apps and bots lose it at once. remove an mcp server and its saved keys are deleted with it.

app sign-ins are held by composio, the service dusk bot uses for connected apps. when a bot uses an app, that request travels through a dusk bot relay to composio and on to the app. the privacy policy has the details.

on this computer, on a dusk cloud computer, or on a server of your own. what each one means and how to choose. your bots have to run somewhere. there are three places, and the app works the same in all of them. you can start in one and move later. {{include ui-where}}

on your computer on dusk cloud on your own server cost free plus or pro free, plus what the server costs you on when your laptop is shut no yes yes where your things are stored your disk your cloud computer your server who looks after it you we do you needs an account no yes no

this is where everyone starts. bots, chats, files and memory stay on your disk. there is no account and nothing to rent. the catch is simple: when your computer sleeps, your bots stop. routines that were due while it slept run late or are skipped.
a computer we host for your bots. routines keep running with your laptop shut. it sleeps when idle and wakes for work. it comes with the plus and pro plans . read more in dusk cloud .
a server you rent and look after yourself. your bots stay on as long as it does. you paste one line and the app sets everything up. read more in your own server .

just trying it, or you only need bots while you work: your computer. you want routines to run overnight and do not want to run a server: dusk cloud. you already rent a server, or want everything on a machine you control: your own server.

the menu at the top of the sidebar is where you switch between This computer and your cloud or server. it is also where you add one. you can keep more than one. some people keep a few bots on their laptop and the always-on ones on a cloud.

when you add a cloud or a server, the app offers to move this computer's bots there, with their chats, memory and routines. after the move they work from the new place, and this computer becomes a window onto it. to move everything by hand, or to keep a copy, use a backup .
wherever your bots live, they use your own ai account. on a cloud or a server you sign in to your ai there once, from your own computer. see connecting an ai .

h: your phone works with all three
x: the phone app pairs with whichever place your bots live. paired with a cloud or a server, it keeps working when your computer is off.

a computer we host for your bots, so routines keep running with your laptop shut. dusk cloud is a computer of your own that we host. your bots live on it and keep working when your laptop is closed. it is part of the plus and pro plans .

plus pro cloud computer 2 vcpu, 4 gb memory, 40 gb disk 4 vcpu, 8 gb memory, 80 gb disk bot computers at once 2 5, first in line to wake work license no yes, for one person a bot computer is a desktop with a browser that a bot can click through and you can watch. see a bot's computer . dusk cloud does not include ai usage. your bots use the ai you sign in with, the same as anywhere else.

pick a plan on the pricing page and check out. this needs an account . in the desktop app, open Settings , Dusk Cloud and sign in. a card says Setting up while your cloud is made. it takes about a minute. when it is ready it shows up as My Cloud , and the card offers Open My Cloud . one click opens it in the app window, signed in. the first time you open it, a short welcome takes you through four steps: bring your st

your cloud needs its own sign-in to your ai, because that is where the bots now think. the welcome shows the same sign-in you saw on your computer. a bot that works around the clock uses your ai plan around the clock. your plan's limits still apply. for heavy use, a bigger ai plan or an api key works best.
a cloud that has nothing to do goes to sleep, and wakes when there is work to do. waking takes a moment. on pro you are first in line.
Settings , Dusk Cloud has a files section with two jobs.

h: share a folder with your cloud
x: choose Add a folder and pick one. the app tells you how many files and how big, and asks before it shares. your cloud gets a read-only copy, kept up to date while this computer is on. bots on the cloud read the copy. they never reach into your computer. your computer's version always wins. a bot cannot change your files. some folders can never be shared: your whole home folder, a whole drive, and folders of keys and

what bots make on the cloud comes down to your computer, into Documents/Dusk Bot , in a folder for each bot and conversation. this is on by default. nothing here is ever deleted because of the cloud. if you edited a file after it came down, the bot's newer version lands beside yours instead of over it.

pair your phone with your cloud instead of your computer and it keeps working while your computer is off. in the desktop app, open the menu under your name, choose Connect your phone , then to the Cloud . see the phone app .

you can cancel from the billing page of your account . bots on your own computer are not affected. the cloud computer is kept for a limited time after the plan ends and is then deleted, so move your bots back or export a backup first. the terms say how long.

keep your bots on a server you rent. paste one line and it installs everything and links itself to your app. if you rent a server, your bots can live there and stay on around the clock. it is free: you pay only for the server. setting it up is one pasted line.

a server running ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 , with 2 gb of memory or more . more memory means more bot computers awake at once. a way to run a command on it as root or as a user who can use sudo . the dusk bot app on your computer. you do not need to open any ports, set up a domain or install anything first. a fresh server is best. give bots a server of their own, not one that also holds things you would not hand to them.

in the app, open the menu at the top of the sidebar, choose Add a Cloud or your own server , and pick your own server. the app shows one line. it works once and for a limited time. log in to your server, paste the line and press return. watch the app. it shows each step as the server sets itself up. {{include ui-server}} the whole thing takes about ten minutes and asks you nothing. it checks the server, installs dock

a step failed: paste the same line again. it is safe to run twice and picks up where it stopped. the line ran out of time: ask the app for a new one. you closed the app: open it again. the server keeps going, and the app catches up.

h: read it before you run it
x: piping a script into a shell deserves a second look. the installer is a plain file you can read first: curl -fsSLo install.sh https://dusk.bot/install.sh curl -fsSL https://dusk.bot/install.sh.sha256 shasum -a 256 install.sh less install.sh the two fingerprints should match. the line the app shows you runs this same script with your one-time code. the script only talks to https addresses and checks the fingerprint of

h: how your app reaches the server
x: your app and your server talk through a small relay at link.dusk.bot . everything they say to each other is sealed with a key that only your app and your server hold, so the relay passes along packages it cannot open. where it can, the app also opens a direct line to your server and uses the relay only as a fallback. you do not configure any of this, and nothing new is opened on the server.

each bot can have its own private desktop on your server, with a browser it signs in to. you can watch it and take control from the app, the same as any bot computer . a desktop nobody is using goes to sleep after about ten minutes and wakes when a bot needs it. how many can be awake at once depends on the server's memory. a server with 12 gb keeps about six awake. desktops are not published to the internet. you see
it is your server, so updates to ubuntu, backups of the disk and the bill are yours. dusk bot runs as a service and starts again by itself after a reboot.
to take dusk bot off a server: curl -fsSL https://link.dusk.bot/uninstall | sh move your bots back to your computer first, or export a backup , if you want to keep them.

text your bots from anywhere. pair your phone with your computer, your server or your cloud by scanning a code. your phone is a window onto your bots. the bots keep running where they live, and the phone lets you text them, answer their questions and get told when they are done.

h: what you can do from your phone
x: read and send messages, to bots and in group chats see a reply arrive as it is written stop a bot answer approvals and questions, so a bot is not stuck waiting for you to get back to your desk

you pair once, by scanning a code. your phone does not need an account. on your computer, open the menu under your name and choose Connect your phone . choose where to connect: to this computer , or to the Cloud if you have one. scan the code with your phone's camera. check the computer's name on the phone and confirm. the phone app is on its way to the app store and google play. until it is there, the code opens dus

h: add it to your home screen
x: iphone: in safari, open the share menu and choose Add to Home Screen . android: in chrome, open the menu and choose Install app or Add to Home screen . if the home screen app asks you to pair again, scan a fresh code. the home screen version does not send notifications and needs a connection to work.

if scanning is not possible, the same screen has other routes: {{include ui-pair}} a code: type a six-digit code shown on the computer. nearby: pick your computer from a list when both are on the same wi-fi. use this only on a network you trust. tailscale: if you already use tailscale, pair over your own private network. the default is Secure HTTPS pairing . it is the simplest, and it keeps working when your phone le

h: your computer has to be awake
x: if your phone is paired with your computer, that computer has to be on, awake and running dusk bot. a sleeping laptop cannot answer your phone. Settings , Remote access has a switch, Keep this computer awake , that stops it sleeping while phone access is on. the screen may still turn off. if you want your phone to work when your computer is off, pair it with dusk cloud or your own server instead.

the phone app from the store sends notifications. when it is closed or in the background, a reply, a question or an approval reaches you as a notification. it shows the bot's name and "new message". the text of the message is not in it, and the service that delivers it never sees the text. while the app is open it shows the message itself, so nothing buzzes twice. the home screen version does not send notifications.

Settings , Remote access lists every device you have paired, and when each was last seen. remove one and it loses access at once. it would have to be paired again. for each device you can also decide whether it may look at a bot's screen.

an account is optional. it shows your workspaces side by side and holds your plan. you do not need an account to use dusk bot on your own computer or your own server. an account at app.dusk.bot is for two things: buying a plan, and seeing all your workspaces in one place.
go to app.dusk.bot and enter your email. we send a code to that address. type it in and you are signed in. there is no password to remember.

a workspace is one place your bots live: your mac, each server, your cloud. the account lists them side by side. for each one you can see: its bots, with their names and which ai each one uses how much work they did each day the machine: processor, memory and disk its bot computers, and whether each is awake the phones and devices paired with it from the same page you can do a few things from afar: wake or sleep a bo

in the desktop app, open the menu under your name and choose Account dashboard . your browser opens. sign in if you are not already. choose Connect . the link is good for one use and for 30 minutes. to disconnect later, remove the workspace from the account. it stops reporting at once.

h: what a workspace tells the account
x: only counts and states. a workspace reports its machine's numbers, bot names, colours and models, the state of its bot computers, device names, and daily usage totals. it never sends messages, prompts, files or keys. your chats stay where your bots live.
plans, invoices and your payment method are on the billing page of your account. see plans and billing .

the account page has Download your data . it gives you one json file with what the account service holds about you. it does not include your chats or files, because the account never had them. for those, make a backup in the app.

the account page has Delete account . it removes the account, your sessions and your linked workspaces. an active plan or a cloud computer has to be cancelled first. the page offers to do that. deleting the account does not delete anything on your own computer or server. it does not close your accounts with your ai providers. those are separate. for anything else about your data, write to privacy@dusk.bot .

where your bots, chats, files and memory are stored, what leaves your machine, and how to back up or delete everything. the short version: your things live where your bots live. on your own computer or server, that means with you. this page is the plain-words map. the privacy policy is the formal one.

your bots live bots, chats, files, memory and settings are on your computer on your disk, in the .duskbot folder in your home folder on your own server on that server on dusk cloud on your cloud computer, which we host dusk cloud is the one case where your content sits on a machine we run. that is what you are choosing when you pick it.

a bot is only useful if it can reach things. here is everything that travels, and to whom. what goes to why what you say to a bot, and its replies the ai provider you signed in to so the ai can think. it goes straight from the machine your bots run on to them. it does not pass through us. what a bot does in a connected app that app, by way of our relay and composio so the bot can read your calendar or draft the email

api keys and sign-ins are kept on the machine your bots run on. after you save a key, the app shows only that one is set. a bot's memory blanks out anything that looks like a password or a key before saving a note.

if you make an account , we store your email address and the things you would expect: your sessions, your linked workspaces and your plan. payments are handled by dodo payments, and we never see your card number. the website and the account use only the cookies they need to keep you signed in. there are no advertising or tracking cookies.

you can take everything with you. open Settings , Backups . choose Export full backup and give it a password of at least 12 characters. keep the file and the password somewhere safe. without the password the backup cannot be opened, by you or by us. the backup holds your bots, conversations, instructions, files and settings. it does not hold your sign-ins or keys. on a new machine you connect your ai and your apps ag

a bot: delete it from the sidebar. its chats and routines go with it. everything on your computer: remove the app and delete the .duskbot folder. a server: run the uninstall line from your own server . your account: use Delete account on the account page. see your account . a cloud computer: it is deleted a limited time after its plan ends. deleting things with us does not delete what your ai provider or a connected
to see, correct or delete what we hold about you, write to privacy@dusk.bot . to report a security problem, write to security@dusk.bot and see the security page .

check these in order: is its ai signed in? open Settings , Model providers . a sign-in can expire. has your plan hit its limit? x: a bot has one screen, and another of its conversations is using it. it carries on by itself when the screen is free. if you took control of the computer, hand it back.

a desktop app where you run a team of ai bots and text them like teammates. each bot has a name, a job, a memory and, if you want, a computer of its own. getting started takes about two minutes.

h: how is this different from a chatbot?
x: a chatbot answers. a bot here has a job it keeps, signs in to your tools, works on a computer, runs on a schedule and remembers how you like things done.
yes, for personal use. the app runs on your computer or your own server with every feature. you only pay for a cloud computer or a work license. see plans and billing .

h: which systems does it run on?
x: macos 12 or later, windows 10 or 11, and ubuntu 24.04. you can text your bots from an iphone or an android phone too. see install and the phone app .
the one you already have. sign in with claude, chatgpt, gemini, grok and others, or add an api key, or use a model you run yourself. see connecting an ai .

h: do i need a paid ai plan?
x: you need some ai to connect: a subscription, an api key or a local model. dusk bot does not come with one.

h: can each bot use a different ai?
x: yes. every bot has its own model, and you can swap it at any time. the bot keeps its chats, files and memory.

h: does dusk bot see what i say to my bots?
x: no. what you say goes straight from the machine your bots run on to your ai provider. see privacy and where data lives .

h: which apps can a bot use?
x: 60+ to start: gmail, google calendar, slack, notion, github, linear, figma, stripe and more. you connect an app once and pick which bots may use it. you can also add any mcp server. see connected apps .

h: is it safe to let bots click around?
x: bots ask before the scary stuff: sending, buying, deleting. you choose how much each bot may do without asking, you can watch it work, and you can take the mouse back at any moment. see permissions and safety .

h: can a bot work while i sleep?
x: yes, with a routine . on your own computer the computer has to be awake. on dusk cloud or your own server, routines run around the clock.
yes. put several in a group chat and they hand work to each other.

h: can i talk to a bot instead of typing?
x: yes. a bot can read its replies aloud, and you can call it. see voice and calls .
nowhere, unless you choose a cloud computer. bots, chats, files and memory live on your machine or your own server.
a computer we host for your bots, so routines keep running when your laptop is closed. see dusk cloud .

h: can i run it on my own server?
x: yes. open the app, add your own server, and paste the line it shows. that is free too. see your own server .
not for the free plan. an account is only for buying a plan and for seeing your workspaces side by side. see your account .

h: can i move my bots later?
x: yes. you can move from your computer to a cloud or a server and back, and you can export a backup of everything at any time.

h: what counts as using it for work?
x: using dusk bot at or for a business. that needs a license. pro includes one for one person, and teams get one with a team plan. the license has the exact words.

h: who bills me for ai usage?
x: your ai provider, on your plan with them. a dusk plan pays for the cloud computer and the license.
any time, from the billing page of your account. see plans and billing .

no. it is source-available, under the polyform strict license: free for personal use, and the license does not allow changing it or passing it on. using it for work needs a separate license. see the license .

h: how do i report a security problem?
x: write to security@dusk.bot . the security page says what to include and what you can expect.
